title: is_valid_mailbox_host allows arbitrary .ts.net hostnames in outbox
description: In kith-peer/lib.rs, is_valid_mailbox_host (used by outbox_tick to validate peer_mailbox_host before delivery) accepts any hostname ending in '.ts.net'. This is intentional per the SSRF design in peer_fetch.rs. However, the outbox function is_valid_mailbox_host has a character-set allowlist (a-z, 0-9, '.', '-', ':') that runs BEFORE the IP-vs-hostname dispatch. The allowlist check includes ':' (needed for [ipv6]:port) in the ip_part character check. But if the input is a bare hostname like 'alice.ts.net', the ip_part is 'alice.ts.net' which contains only alphanumeric and '.', so it passes. Then it fails IpAddr::parse, and hits the ends_with('.ts.net') check. This is correct. BUT: the character-set check for bare hostnames allows ':' in the hostname part (ip_part allowlist includes b':'). A malformed input like 'alice.ts.net:evil' with port 'evil' is caught by the port parse failing (returns false). So the character allowlist for hostnames is over-permissive (allows ':') but the port validation provides the safety net. This is a footgun: future maintainers may assume the character allowlist is the primary guard, not the secondary port check.
